correctness.rationale: For all q>=3,a,b>=1, direct first-side recolouring gives delta H=B_j-B_i and second-side gives A_j-A_i. Any shared colour forces every opposite-side multiplicity strictly positive, hence both sides contain every colour and both vectors are uniform. A two-site cross swap changes H by -2; all proper colourings have H=0. Exact onto/multinomial count and fixed-q Stirling with dominant s(q-s) yield both sublimits and nonexistence. Independent direct-edge-energy exhaustive program passed 50 cases, 25,300 assignments and 1,986 two-move comparisons; no finite test is used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Prior papers define the same local best-response condition (Kun et al.) and standard proper-colouring Potts ground states (Sokal); the public majority-C result independently covers the binary equal-part split under an opposite inequality. The new claim is the all-q>=3 complete-bipartite exact energy-resolved blocked-state classification, its strict two-site collapse, and size-divisibility-dependent failure of the normalized blocked entropy limit. No inspected stronger theorem implies that full conjunctive statement. An unindexed game-theoretic treatment remains a genuine risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed complete-bipartite anti-coordination Nash-equilibrium count could imply the same structural criterion or arithmetic entropy without matching terminology; search absence cannot certify independence.
The two-colour balanced-slice multinomial count is already found in a different same-colour-majority setting; the novelty claim is expressly restricted to q>=3 and the conjunctive Potts result.
No independent human literature audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The natural all-q>=3 full blocked-energy invariant of a Potts antiferromagnet has an exceptional arithmetic entropy spike: the high-energy local minima dominate exponentially many configurations at q-divisible symmetric graph sizes, vanish completely at adjacent sizes, and can all be escaped by a two-vertex cooperative recolouring. This is a structural positive-energy-versus-proper classification with a macroscopic entropy discontinuity along size subsequences, not a small numerical optimization or arbitrary parameter slice. Its scope is explicitly restricted to downhill dynamics; generic one-site Nash stability is acknowledged as prior.
